# Control Narrative: Kiln Baghouse BH-700

**Status: DRAFT. Not ready for programming until the open items in Section 9 are resolved.**
Source: operating practice described by shift supervisor (Dave). Values marked **[TBC-n]** are proposed defaults or gaps that need sign-off from operations, process engineering, and the bag/equipment vendors.

---

## 1. Scope

This section covers the automatic start, run, cleaning, protection, and shutdown of baghouse BH-700, which serves the kiln exhaust.

## 2. Equipment and Instruments

| Tag | Description | Signals Required |
|---|---|---|
| SC-701 | Dust discharge screw conveyor | Start/stop, run feedback, zero-speed switch **[TBC-1]** |
| RV-702 | Hopper rotary airlock | Start/stop, run feedback, zero-speed switch **[TBC-1]** |
| F-703 | ID fan | Start/stop, run feedback |
| D-704 | Inlet damper | Open/close command, open and closed limit switches |
| TT-705 | Baghouse inlet temperature | 4–20 mA, °F |
| D-706 | Bleed-air (tempering) damper | Open/close command, limit switches (or modulating, **[TBC-2]**) |
| PDT-7xx | Baghouse differential pressure (tag not provided) | 4–20 mA, in. WC **[TBC-3]** |
| Pulse controller | Solenoid valves, row sequencing | Interval setpoint, enable, fault |
| — | Kiln feed | Interlock output to kiln feed system **[TBC-4]** |

## 3. Operating Modes

- **Auto:** Sequences in Sections 4–7 run from a single Start/Stop command.
- **Manual:** Individual equipment control from the HMI for maintenance. Safety interlocks in Section 6 stay active in all modes.

## 4. Start Sequence

**Permissives (all must be true before Start is accepted):**
- No active trips on BH-700 equipment
- D-704 proven closed
- Pulse controller healthy, compressed air pressure OK **[TBC-5]**

**Sequence:**

| Step | Action | Proceed When |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Start SC-701 | SC-701 run feedback (and motion proven) within 10 s **[TBC-6]** |
| 2 | Start RV-702 | RV-702 run feedback (and motion proven) within 10 s **[TBC-6]** |
| 3 | Start F-703 with D-704 closed | F-703 run feedback within 30 s **[TBC-6]** |
| 4 | Fan stabilization timer | Timer complete, 60 s **[TBC-7]** |
| 5 | Open D-704 | D-704 open limit within 60 s **[TBC-6]** |
| 6 | Enable pulse cleaning at normal interval (Section 5) | — |
| 7 | Set "BH-700 Running" permissive to kiln feed | — |

If any step fails to prove within its timeout, the sequence aborts and performs a normal shutdown (Section 7) with an alarm identifying the failed step.

> **Note on start order:** The supervisor reported that some operators start F-703 before SC-701/RV-702. This narrative uses a single fixed order: the discharge path first (conveyor, then airlock), then the fan. That way dust always has a proven path out of the hopper before gas flow begins. **[TBC-8]**: operations must confirm this order. The programmed sequence will not support both orders.

## 5. Normal Operation: Pulse Cleaning

Pulse cleaning fires one row at a time, in sequence, on a timed interval selected by baghouse DP.

| Condition | Pulse Interval |
|---|---|
| DP < 6.0 in. WC | 10 s per row (normal) |
| DP ≥ 6.0 in. WC | 5 s per row (high-rate) |
| Return to normal | DP < 5.0 in. WC for 60 s **[TBC-9]** |

- Interval setpoints and DP thresholds must be adjustable from the HMI with supervisor-level access.
- If the DP transmitter fails (signal out of range), default to the 5 s interval and alarm.

## 6. Alarms and Interlocks

### 6.1 Differential Pressure

| Condition | Setpoint | Action |
|---|---|---|
| DP High | 6.0 in. WC | Alarm; switch to high-rate pulsing (Section 5) |
| DP High-High | 8.0 in. WC, 30 s delay **[TBC-10]** | Alarm and **stop kiln feed** **[TBC-4], [TBC-10]** |

### 6.2 Inlet Temperature (TT-705)

| Condition | Setpoint | Action |
|---|---|---|
| Temp High | 450 °F | Alarm; open D-706 |
| Temp Normal | < 425 °F for 60 s **[TBC-11]** | Close D-706 |
| Temp High-High | **[TBC-12]** | Alarm, stop kiln feed, close D-704 **[TBC-12]** |

If D-706 fails to reach the commanded position within 30 s, raise an alarm.

### 6.3 Discharge Equipment Failure (Hopper Overfill / Fire Risk)

The supervisor reported a 2019 hopper fire linked to airlock stoppage. This interlock is safety-related.

| Trigger | Action |
|---|---|
| RV-702 loss of run feedback or zero-speed while commanded on | **Immediate trip:** stop kiln feed, close D-704, stop pulse cleaning, alarm. Fan action **[TBC-13]** |
| SC-701 loss of run feedback or zero-speed while commanded on | Stop RV-702 (so it does not discharge onto a stopped screw), then perform the RV-702 trip actions above **[TBC-14]** |

- Trips latch and require operator reset at the HMI after the cause is cleared.
- **[TBC-15]:** The hazard analysis should decide whether a hopper high-level switch and/or a hopper temperature or spark detection should be added as independent protection.

### 6.4 Fan Failure

| Trigger | Action |
|---|---|
| F-703 loss of run feedback while commanded on | Stop kiln feed, close D-704, alarm. Keep SC-701/RV-702 running to clear the hopper. |

## 7. Normal Shutdown Sequence

| Step | Action | Proceed When |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Remove "BH-700 Running" permissive; confirm kiln feed stopped **[TBC-16]** | Kiln feed stopped |
| 2 | Close D-704 | D-704 closed limit |
| 3 | Clean-down: F-703 running, pulse cleaning continues at the normal interval | 10 min timer complete |
| 4 | Stop pulse cleaning | — |
| 5 | Stop F-703 | — |
| 6 | Hopper clear-out: SC-701 and RV-702 keep running | Clear-out timer, **[TBC-17]** |
| 7 | Stop RV-702 | — |
| 8 | Stop SC-701 | — |

> **[TBC-18]:** The email says to pulse "with the fan running" during clean-down. Confirm whether D-704 should be closed (as drafted above) or open during clean-down. With the damper closed, airflow through the bags may be minimal.

## 8. HMI Requirements (Minimum)

- Equipment status, DP, TT-705, damper positions, current pulse interval
- Sequence step indication and active timers
- Adjustable setpoints (supervisor access): pulse intervals, DP thresholds, temperature thresholds, timers
- Alarm and trip history with first-out indication

## 9. Open Items: Must Be Resolved Before Programming

| # | Item | Owner |
|---|---|---|
| TBC-1 | Are zero-speed/motion switches installed on SC-701 and RV-702? Run feedback alone will not detect a sheared shaft or a jammed rotor with the motor still running. | Maintenance / E&I |
| TBC-2 | Is D-706 on/off or modulating? If modulating, a temperature control loop replaces the on/off logic. | E&I |
| TBC-3 | DP transmitter tag and range. | E&I |
| TBC-4 | Kiln feed interlock: hardwired or networked? Which signal stops feed? | Process / E&I |
| TBC-5 | Is there a compressed-air pressure switch for the pulse system? | E&I |
| TBC-6 | Proving timeouts for each device. | Integrator / Maintenance |
| TBC-7 | Fan stabilization time. The email says "a minute or so"; 60 s is proposed. | Operations |
| TBC-8 | Start order. Conveyor/airlock first vs. fan first. One must be chosen. | Operations / Process |
| TBC-9 | DP reset point and hysteresis for returning to normal pulsing. | Process |
| TBC-10 | DP High-High: the email says "6 or 7" for high-rate and "usually" stops feed above 8. Confirm exact setpoints and whether the feed stop is automatic or an operator alarm only. | Operations / Process |
| TBC-11 | Temperature reset point for closing D-706. | Process |
| TBC-12 | Bag maximum temperature rating (from the bag vendor), the High-High setpoint, and the action taken. | Process / Bag vendor |
| TBC-13 | On airlock trip, should F-703 stop (reducing oxygen to a possible hopper fire) or keep running? This needs a deliberate fire-hazard decision, not a default. | Process Safety |
| TBC-14 | Confirm the conveyor-failure cascade logic. | Process |
| TBC-15 | Hazard review of the 2019 fire: are additional safeguards required (level, temperature, spark detection, SIL assessment)? | Process Safety |
| TBC-16 | Does BH-700 shutdown command the kiln feed off, or only require it to be off as a permissive? | Operations |
| TBC-17 | Hopper clear-out run time after fan stop. | Operations |
| TBC-18 | Damper position during the 10-minute clean-down. | Operations / Process |

---

**Recommendation:** Review Sections 6.3 and 9 (TBC-13, TBC-15) with process safety before this goes to the integrator. Given the prior fire, the airlock-failure response should be engineered, not inferred from an email.
